The relation of the Will to Him is like the relation of the House to God - it is a relation bestowing honor upon creation, not unto the Essence, for He is sanctified above the mention of allusions, relations, indications, signs, stations, effulgences and fragrances attributed to Him.

order.why: Consider the limits of reasoning from contingent knowledge to divine knowledge.
shortened: Never will the spiders of vain imaginings weave their web upon the branches of the knowledge of the reality of the Almighty, Omniscient One; nor will the flea in the dust circle about the stars of the heavenly spheres.  How can the reality of non-existence ever understand the ipseity of being?  How can utter annihilation [fana] be informed of the essence of eternity [baqa]?  For the subtleties of the realities of essences of Possible Being have been created by a word of His Command and one of His Verses and have come into being through one ray of the effulgences of the Sun of His Will.

order.why: Keep the sea and waves within the account of the Primal Will.
shortened: As to the station of the Godhead, it is exalted above and sanctified beyond the understanding of all created things, how much more above resolving itself into their realities!  His Holiness the Bab (may my life be a sacrifice unto Him) hath stated that the meaning of the verse "The sea hath ever been the sea, and all contingent things its waves and forms" is fulfilled in the Primal Will, not in the Divine Essence.
Rather is it the Primal Will, which consisteth of the radiance and bounties of that Sun, that causeth the manifestation, appearance, and visibility of all beings.

order.why: Read the distinction among the worlds of Truth, Command, and creation.
shortened: But in the view of the Prophets it is not so. Rather, through proofs and evidences they established a third realm: the world of Truth [Haqq; also God], the world of Command, and the world of creation.

The world of Command is the station of the Primal Will which is a universal reality that is resolved into infinite forms. This is the reality of existence that is comprehended and understood by the human world. As for the world of creation, it consists of the infinite forms of that sea of Will which is the world of Command.

order.why: Consider the critique of philosophical explanations of the first emanation.
Read correspondence and servitude in the account of the Will’s formation.
Consider origination without a preceding created thing.
shortened: From it all things were fashioned, through it all things were called into being, upon it all things were founded, and within it all things found their establishment. Through it was the Divine Will brought into being before the mention of thingness, and in it was Lordship made manifest and all servitude made firm. It is neither of the eternal East nor of the non-existent West. It came into being through its own essence, not from any creation before it, and was endowed with its identity without any invention to rival it.

order.why: Read the beginning of the Will beside the capacity bestowed upon it.
shortened: The beginning of the existence of the Primal Will--which is the Cause of causes and the ultimate light of the Eternal Morn--was but from nothing, as You manifested unto it through itself, and it was established in its shadow.
You bestowed upon it what it could bear of what it would create through itself.

order.why: Distinguish existence and quiddity in the account of Will and Volition.
shortened: God, moreover, hath brought forth the Primal Will from nothing, by naught but itself -- as the Imam hath alluded, and his word is the truth -- for every "thing" must needs possess existence: this is the rank of Will in its own realm; and (then) it must have a "quiddity": this is the rank of Volition in its own degree; and the nexus between them is the world of Decree and the secret of possibility in its station.

order.why: Read the Will within the realm of possibility.
Consider the Point creating through an unending succession.
Read the denial of an additional cause beyond origination itself.
Keep the numbered letter and quoted testimony within the commentary’s symbolic setting.
Connect the account of the Will with the Point of the Bayan.
Read creation from nothingness beside the limits of signs.
shortened: No sign can indicate His presence or His absence; inasmuch as by a word of His command all that are in heaven and on earth have come to exist, and by His wish, which is the Primal Will itself, all have stepped out of utter nothingness into the realm of being, the world of the visible.

order.why: Consider the creature’s inability to encompass its Creator.
Hear the praise of creative power in the Qayyumu’l-Asma.
Read one source for creation and the Word as the wellspring of intellect.
Bring the metaphysical inquiry toward humanity’s shared world and origin.
shortened: Ye dwell in one world, and have been created through the operation of one Will.

order.why: Consider knowledge and love as creation’s purpose.
shortened: Having created the world and all that liveth and moveth therein, He, through the direct operation of His unconstrained and sovereign Will, chose to confer upon man the unique distinction and capacity to know Him and to love Him -- a capacity that must needs be regarded as the generating impulse and the primary purpose underlying the whole of creation, as mentioned in the well-known sacred tradition.

order.why: Read every atom as participating in human training.
Consider intellect and wisdom through their transforming effects.
Read arts and knowledge through the creative divine names.
shortened: When the sun of His name, the Creator, dawneth from the horizon of His mouth, through it are made manifest the arts throughout all ages - this is an indubitable truth.

Likewise, when the sun of My name, the All-Knowing, dawneth from the horizon of utterance, every thing receiveth from this Name the wondrous knowledge according to its capacity and measure, and there appeareth therefrom in these days by the command of the Mighty, the All-Knowing.

order.why: Consider fuller receptivity through humanity’s development.
shortened: Therefore, a spirit has emanated from the reality of Divinity, and its effulgences have become visible in human entities or realities.

The more the world of humanity develops, the more the effulgences or emanations of Divinity will become revealed, just as the stone, when it becomes polished and pure as a mirror, will reflect in fuller degree the glory and splendor of the sun.

order.why: Keep the explanation of a pantheistic statement within its account of energy and bounty.
Read the reported language of development and fusion in its own source setting.
shortened: The Primal Will operates in the element, in the primal atom, as attraction and repulsion; on the next higher level as organic life; then as animal-vegetative; and finally as spiritual life, which is destined to rise to the super-spiritual. What develops is not the physical substratum (base), which actually exists from the beginning in its different kinds, each of which then develops only within its own kind to higher perfection, but rather does the Cosmic Spirit, the divine Primal Will, unfold within the creature just as the bud of a flower unfolds ever more completely, purely and beautifully, and will finally, in the fully-redeemed, totally purified man, return to the Godhead, to be immersed and fused in the Godhead.

order.why: Consider the concise claim concerning choice in genesis and law.
Read the invitation to apprehend divine purpose.
shortened: Happy is the man that hath apprehended the Purpose of God in whatever He hath revealed from the Heaven of His Will that pervadeth all created things.

order.why: Keep the prayer’s account of opposition in its particular voice.
shortened: Thereby have Thy servants, who were created through the word of Thy commandment, and were begotten by Thy will, caviled at me, and so fiercely opposed me that they repudiated Thee, and have rejected Thy signs, and have risen up against Thee.

order.why: Hear the affirmation of unconstrained divine sovereignty.
Consider the limits encountered even in praise of wisdom and oneness.
Close the linked sequence with humility expressed as prayer for mercy.
shortened: Inasmuch as Thou hast ordained that the utmost limit to which they who lift their hearts to Thee can rise is the confession of their powerlessness to enter the realms of Thy holy and transcendent unity, and that the highest station which they who aspire to know Thee can reach is the acknowledgement of their impotence to attain the retreats of Thy sublime knowledge, I, therefore, beseech Thee, by this very powerlessness which is beloved of Thee, and which Thou hast decreed as the goal of them that have reached and attained Thy court, and by the splendours of Thy countenance that have encompassed all things, and by the energies of Thy Will whereby the entire creation hath been generated, not to deprive them that have set their hopes in Thee of the wonders of Thy mercy, nor to withhold from such as have sought Thee the treasures of Thy grace.

order.why: Read the supplied provisional formulation of creation through the Primal Will.
Consider the supplied tradition concerning the Will’s own self.
Read the supplied distinction of self-cause and subsequent effects.
Examine the fuller provisional discussion of causation and divine knowledge.
shortened: God, verily, created the Will from nothing through itself, then He created through it all that to which the name "thing" can be applied. The cause of its existence, in truth, is its own self and naught else. Those who believe that the Essence is the cause of creation have made themselves partners with Him, as He cannot be known. He, verily, abideth in a state accessible only to Himself. Nothing is connected to Him, and in Him not a trace of the existence belonging to created things can be found. It is established in philosophy that cause and effect are alike. Therefore, the Imam hath declared: "The cause of things is His fashioning, but He is not its cause."

To establish God's knowledge of His creatures can only lead to falsehood, since from time immemorial God's knowledge hath been the same as Himself without another object of knowledge within Him. No one can understand the state of His Being except Himself.

order.why: Read the supplied argument against attributing created causation to the essence.
shortened: Verily God hath intended by these exalted words to sanctify His Essence utterly from any attribute of causation, refuting the views of those who have considered the Essence to be the Cause of all causes. For, verily, that Cause is His Handiwork, and that Handiwork is not preceded by any cause, to such an extent that the tongue of His favoured ones repeatedly addressed this absence of causation by the Essence. Had it been the Essence that was also the Cause, this would have required association and resemblance.
He hath fashioned the Will from nothingness, through Itself, and ordained It to be the Cause of all that is other than It, with no descent of anything from His Essence unto the Will.

order.why: Consider the related critique of fixed archetypes and causal resemblance.
shortened: The statement of the philosophers that the cause of the created beings is the Essence is erroneous because of the lack of association [between cause and effect], the utter impossibility of change, and the precondition of the resemblance of the cause and the effect. The truth is that the Cause of beings is God's Handiwork, created by God Himself for Himself, and ordained to be the Cause of all His creation.

order.why: Read the limits of created praise beside the source of origination.
Retain the supplied description of the Originator of causes with its reference status.
Consider Shaykh Ahmad’s distinction between an action and the materials of its result.
Read the supplied Plotinus passage within its accompanying references.
Consider the supplied image of radiation from an unchanged source.
Read Augustine’s distinction between a created beginning and a beginning in time.
Retain the supplied provisional excerpt concerning the agency of the Will.
Read the separate supplied formulation from the commentary on all food.
Consider the concise supplied affirmation of creation through Will.
Read fire and heat as an image of intimate dependence.
Hear the supplied prayer concerning the Will’s pervasive influence.
Return from origin to knowledge and observance.
End with the attributed secondary reflection on devotion and the limits of mystical attainment.

questions: How might something depend upon a source without beginning at an earlier or later moment?
What distinctions are protected by calling the Primal Will created while describing it as its own cause?
How do sun, mirror, sea, and waves help the inquiry, and where do these images reach their limits?
How does Augustine’s distinction between created wisdom and divine Wisdom sharpen the comparison concerning origin before time?
What is gained by distinguishing a passage’s philosophical argument, devotional voice, and source status?
How might the limits of understanding become an invitation to knowledge, love, and purposeful action rather than an end to inquiry?

references.label: 1 · Augustine, Confessions XII.15.20 · A created beginning before time
references.note: In Book XII, chapter 15, paragraph 20, Augustine distinguishes created intellectual wisdom from the divine Wisdom he regards as co-eternal with God. The created wisdom has an origin even though no time precedes it. Compare that distinction with the compilation’s account of essential rather than temporal origination. The comparison concerns a problem of dependence and time; it does not identify Augustine’s created wisdom with the Primal Will.

subjects.displayTitle: Hands of the Cause: distinction expressed through service
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh named as Hands of His Cause those souls who had given up their own will, who harboured no thought of self and stood firm in service; ‘Abdu’l-Bahá added that it is not a title to be handed out or a chair of honour to be sat in, but that whoever serves the Word of God is a hand of God. Their duties are to diffuse the divine fragrances, edify souls, promote learning and improve character; the same instructions turn practical in a moment, settling a pharmacist’s bill or securing a modest living for a Hand in straitened circumstances. Appointments, temporary arrangements with assemblies and later statements about rank belong to different seasons of an institution’s growth, and each asks to be read in its own occasion. Peter’s counsel that those who tend a flock should do so willingly and by example, not as lords over it, offers a kindred ethic of service [1]. The path continues through Shoghi Effendi and the Guardianship, under whose direction the Hands were appointed and set to the defence and spread of the Faith.
subjects.arc: Begin with selfless service and learning, examine unity and protection, and read institutional responsibilities within their historical development.

order.why: Read the duties and institutional provisions in the Will and Testament.
shortened: O friends! The Hands of the Cause of God must be nominated and appointed by the Guardian of the Cause of God. All must be under his shadow and obey his command.

The obligations of the Hands of the Cause of God are to diffuse the Divine Fragrances, to edify the souls of men, to promote learning, to improve the character of all men and to be, at all times and under all conditions, sanctified and detached from earthly things. They must manifest the fear of God by their conduct, their manners, their deeds and their words.
This body of the Hands of the Cause of God is under the direction of the Guardian of the Cause of God.

order.why: Open with selflessness and steadfast service.
shortened: These are the Hands of the Cause among mankind, and these are the souls who, having abandoned their own will and desire, have held fast to the Will and Purpose of God. They harbor no thoughts of self, and stand firm in service and in offering praise and glorification to the Self-Sufficient, the Most High.

order.why: Define the work through education and the reform of the world.
Connect honor with those who arise to reform the world.
shortened: Yet the people of the earth remain heedless and veiled, save for a numbered few who are the Hands of the Cause among His servants. In truth, praise and glorification today befit these souls who have arisen to reform the world and are confirmed in that which exalteth the Word of God.

order.why: Consider learning, writing, and reasoned explanation as forms of service.
Retain the concise description of the Hands as educators.
shortened: The Hands of the Cause of God have been and are the educators of the servants.

order.why: Read teaching love, piety, and fellowship as signs of servitude.
Keep the reported emphasis on spirit and service distinct from a merely honorary title.
shortened: It is not a title to be bestowed upon whomsoever they wish, nor a seat to which anyone who desireth may become heir. The "Hands of the Cause" are the hands of God. Thus whosoever is the helper and servant of the Word of God, he is the hand of God.

order.why: Read the written explanation of appointment and firmness in the Covenant.
Relate respect to those described as foremost in service.
shortened: It behoveth every one of you, however, to show the utmost consideration unto the revered Hands who are foremost in service, for they are the dawning-places of the manifold bounties, loving-kindness, and favours of the Blessed Beauty.

order.why: Describes the Hands’ role in meeting communities’ needs for teachers.
Make material care part of that respect.
Read the particular instruction concerning Ibn-i-Abhar’s debts and support.
shortened: And regarding His Honor the Hand of the Cause Ibn-i-Abhar, upon him be the Most Glorious Splendor - definitely pay his debts immediately, including the hundred tomans to Aqa Ghulam-'Ali the pharmacist, and likewise give him all his allowances to date without any reduction, and show the utmost love and respect.

order.why: Consider the referred family matter within its practical setting.
shortened: Whatever the Hands of the Cause deem advisable is the very truth and must be carried out.
Today, whatever the Hands of the Cause deem advisable is implemented by this servant.
In any case, so that this family may not become completely dejected and despairing, this matter is being referred to the Hands regarding whatever manner they deem advisable to implement.

order.why: Read the call for unity through obedience to the Hands’ decisions.
Consider agreement and majority decision in the historical account.
shortened: The Hands of the Cause of God are like brilliant lamps. Whatever decision they make, or agreement they reach, or majority vote they achieve, all must obey and submit.

order.why: Read referral to the assembly in the presence of the Hands.
shortened: Therefore, whenever any of the friends conceives of an idea or brings an important matter to mind, they must refer it to the assembly in the presence of the Hands of the Cause - upon them be the Glory of God, His praise, His might, and His exaltation. If the Hands approve it, then it may be carried out; if not, then no.

order.why: Keep the specific arrangement for an assembly’s membership in its setting.
Consider consultation and majority decision in the restoration of a sacred resting place.
shortened: If you deem it advisable, this matter could be discussed in Tehran at the spiritual gathering of the Hands of the Cause of God. Whatever you consider appropriate and suitable to the time, place and circumstances, implement it by majority vote. For if matters, especially in the gathering of the Hands of the Cause of God, are not decided upon, that gathering will become completely weak and foundationless, and many problems will arise.

order.why: Read the explicit temporary character of the assembly arrangement.
Keep the instruction on permanent membership within its historical occasion.
Read membership and voting rights in that institutional context.
shortened: The Hands of the Cause of God, upon them be the Most Glorious Glory of God, are among the original members and pillars of the Spiritual Assembly and have voting rights.

order.why: Retain the related instruction concerning membership.
Hear the stated duty of consideration and respect.
Read the particular counsel to follow the Hands’ advice.
Connect obedience with a life renewed through divine bounty.
shortened: You who are signs of the favors of the Luminary of the horizons must illumine the world and show obedience to the Hands of the Cause of God, and in every breath be alive and refreshed through the sweet-scented breaths of the Abha Kingdom.

order.why: Make the Hands’ own unity part of their protective responsibility.
shortened: O Hands of the Cause! Gather together and unite, and become as one spirit, one soul, one body, one heart and one mind. Do not allow anyone to create a breach in the Cause of God or introduce any weakness.

order.why: Read the duty of protection during Abdu’l-Baha’s absence.
shortened: In brief, during 'Abdu'l-Baha's absence, the Hands of the Cause of God must protect the Cause of God so that it remains preserved and safeguarded from all contingencies.

order.why: Consider protection through the promise of divine assistance.
Read steadfastness through the contrast of passing foam and lasting benefit.
shortened: However, those Hands of the Cause of God should be assured that these matters are like the foam on a flood: "As for the foam, it vanishes as scum upon the banks, while that which benefits mankind remains on earth." Through the protection, preservation and confirmation of the Ancient Beauty, I hope that the Hands of the Cause of God, may the glory of God be upon them, will, like bars of iron, protect the mighty fortress of the Cause from the attack of others.

order.why: Examine the language of guardianship and protection in its source setting.
shortened: Through His prevailing Will, He hath established the edifice of His Cause upon the foundation of exposition and the elements of explanation, and hath created for it guardians and protectors to preserve it from every heedless betrayer and ignorant speaker - they who transgress not what God hath revealed in the Book and who speak naught except that which He hath permitted them in the final abode. I bear witness that they are the Hands of His Cause amidst all creation and the Lamps of His guidance between earth and heaven. They are they who stand at His gate and drive away such as are unworthy to enter His court.

order.why: Join protection with the energetic spread of the teachings.
shortened: The Hands of the Cause of God, upon them be praise, upon them be glory, upon them be bounty and bestowal, must show forth tremendous power and the might of Gabriel in teaching the Cause of God and promoting the religion of God, so that 'Abdu'l-Baha may be assured of the spread of the divine fragrances in the East.

order.why: Read teaching as strengthening the divine edifice.
shortened: The Hands of the Cause of God, upon them be the Most Glorious Glory of God, their greatest duty today is to diffuse the divine fragrances, for through this the divine edifice becomes firm and solid.

order.why: Consider time and opportunity as precious trusts.
shortened: The time must be regarded as precious, and opportunity must not be lost. Therefore the Hands of the Cause of God must devote all their time to teaching.

order.why: Keep the criticism of a particular Tehran dispute distinct from a general rejection of assemblies.
Read the fire imagery as spiritual attraction and guidance.
Hear the encouragement to increase in joy and strength.
shortened: The Hands of the Cause of God must always strive in such matters so that divine confirmations may surround from all directions. At every moment they should gain joy and fragrance and increase in strength and power.

order.why: Read the personal news of Abdu’l-Baha’s health and continuing service.
shortened: Upon hearing this news, through the assistance and bounty of the Blessed Beauty, health was suddenly restored and I immediately set about writing this letter so that the Hands of the Cause of God may give the glad tidings to all the friends that 'Abdu'l-Baha is not weak - through the assistance, bounty, grace and confirmation of the Ancient Beauty He is supremely powerful, and proof of this is that night and day He is occupied with writing and speaking.

order.why: Consider mutual prayer and the example of sacrifice.
shortened: O ye Hands of the Cause! Supplicate ye and pray on my behalf as I do pray on yours that a heavenly power, a divine bounty, a celestial assistance, and victory from on high be vouchsafed on us all and that we may be aided to achieve that which is seemly and necessary to promulgate the Divine light towards the east and towards the west and like those holy souls who attained the sheltering shadow of Jesus Christ we may sacrifice ourselves and recall at all times how our Beloved One suffered afflictions and torments and persecutions with such constancy and how often He became chained and fettered so that He might save us poor ones and enable us lowly ones to attain honour and glory in His Kingdom.

order.why: Read steadfastness in a biographical portrait.
shortened: Openly at odds with his tyrannical oppressors, no matter how often they threatened him, he defied them. He was never vanquished. Whatever he had to say, he said. He was one of the Hands of the Cause of God, steadfast, unshakable, not to be moved.

order.why: Keep the reported tribute to constancy attributed.
shortened: He became one of the Hands of the Cause of God and was steadfast in the Covenant with perfect firmness and constancy.

order.why: Read the particular recognition of an Afnan and Hand of the Cause.
shortened: Through God's grace - exalted be His glory - thou art mentioned and recorded in the Book as one of the Afnans of the Tree and as one of the Hands of the Cause.

order.why: Consider the instruction to share a visitation prayer.
shortened: O Hands of the Cause of God! This visitation prayer should be recited by me along with a group of the loved ones of God at the fragrant resting place of that promulgator of God's Cause on a special day, and you should disseminate this visitation prayer among all the loved ones.

order.why: Read the visitation blessing through the image of hands that manifest divine power.
shortened: The peace that hath shone forth from the Dayspring of the Will of God, the Lord of all being, and the light that hath dawned above the horizon of His supreme mercy and His resplendent signs rest upon you, O ye who are the hands of His power in the kingdom of creation and the manifestations of His grandeur between earth and heaven!

order.why: Read remembrance through the repair of graves.
Recognize companionship on a journey as part of this history of service.
shortened: O herald of the Kingdom! Give thanks to God that in this journey you traveled with Mr. Harris, the herald of the Kingdom of the All-Merciful, and became companions with His Holiness Ibn-i-Abhar, Hand of the Cause of God, and became confidants with the faithful servant at the Threshold of Baha, Aqa Mirza Mahmud.

order.why: Hear the address to two faithful helpers.
shortened: O two faithful servants of Truth and two helpers of the Covenant and two Hands of the Cause of the luminous horizons!

order.why: Retain the particular greeting to the friends.
Read praise through the themes of fortitude and divine bounty.
Consider the related praise of patience and grace.
shortened: Light and glory, magnification and praise be upon the Hands of His Cause, through whom the light of patience hath shone forth and the ordinance of choice been established - God, the Powerful, the Mighty, the Choosing. Through them the ocean of bounty hath surged and the fragrance of God's tender mercy, the Lord of all beings, hath been wafted.

order.why: Read steadfastness amid opposition.
Consider courage that continues despite outward power.
Read remembrance and obedience amid ordinary occupations.
shortened: These are they whom God hath described in His mighty Book, both aforetime and in these days: "Men whom neither merchandise nor traffic beguile from the remembrance of God," and in another passage: "They speak not until He hath spoken, and they do as they are bidden." Through them hath God revealed His Cause and His sovereignty, through them hath He guided mankind unto His straight Path and His mighty Announcement, and through them have His traces been spread abroad, His signs been exalted, and His lights been manifested.

order.why: Connect service with fidelity to the Covenant.
Hear dedication and the prayer for further assistance.
shortened: Praise be to God that despite the turning away of the world and the blindness of the nations, the Hands of the Cause of God are arising with complete dedication to serve the Cause, and are, despite the enemies, drinking from the Kawthar of eternity in the Most Great Name.

I beseech Thee by the mysteries hidden in Thy verses and by the lights shining from the horizon of Thy manifestation, to ordain for each one of the Hands of Thy Cause that which will enable them to raise the standards of Thy guidance among Thy creatures and the banners of Thy victory in Thy lands.

order.why: Read traveling to share the teachings.
Consider travel, fidelity, and the sharing of recognition.
Read wisdom and utterance flowing through service across lands.
Retain the related praise of travel and steadfastness.
shortened: And peace and blessings be upon the Hands of His Cause who have traversed the lands to exalt His Word, who have not violated His Covenant and Testament, and who have attained unto the choice wine of revelation in His days. These are among the most exalted of creatures in His Book.

order.why: Consider service through the image of keys to knowledge.
Read the giving of divine knowledge amid religions.
shortened: These are the Hands of His Cause amongst mankind and the cupbearers of the Salsabil of divine knowledge amidst all religions.

order.why: Consider the Hands as guides and lamps.
Read bounty shared with seekers without a self-directed purpose.
Join the images of hands and lamps with love and understanding.
Consider leaves and fruits guided by divine Will.
shortened: These are the Hands of God's Cause amongst creation, and these are the trees in the divine garden, their leaves moved by His will and their fruits manifested through His decree.

order.why: Read rain and growth as images of service’s effects.
Hear the praise of wisdom and utterance.
Keep honor joined to piety and freedom from wrongdoing.
Read recognition of the Day of God and illumined hearts.
Consider renewed life and detachment.
Hear the joy brought by news of a gathering of the Hands.
shortened: In the letter of the beloved of the heart, mention was made of the gathering of the Hands of the Cause, upon them be the Glory of God, the Most Glorious, in that land, and great joy and delight were expressed at this matter.

order.why: Keep the blessing in its particular religious address.
Read the appeal to assist the Wronged One.
Hear the prayer that servants may spread the signs of sovereignty.
shortened: Enable them, then, to become the Hands of Thy Cause amongst Thy servants, that they may scatter abroad Thy signs, and show forth Thy sovereignty.

order.why: Read the prayer of blessing upon their service.
Join praise with a prayer for preservation and assistance.
Consider detachment and righteousness in the language of blessing.
shortened: O my God! Send down Thy blessings upon the Hands of Thy Cause, whose heads Thou hast adorned with the crowns of detachment and whose temples Thou hast arrayed with the robes of righteousness and fear of God, and whom Thou hast preserved from transgression and immorality.

order.why: Read the request to convey greetings personally.
Hear the greeting after strife gives way to peace.
Close the linked sequence with a prayer for assistance.
shortened: O my Lord! Assist the hands of Thy Cause with hosts rushing forth from Thy Kingdom and stars rising from Thy Dominion and lions roaring in the thickets of Thy Lordship.

order.why: Read the supplied reported account of humility and service beyond titles.
shortened: It is not a title that may be awarded to whomsoever it pleases, nor is it a chair of honour in which whomsoever pleases sits. The Hands of the Cause are Hands of God. Hence whosoever is the servant and the promoter of the Word of God, he is the Hand of God. The object is the spirit and not the letters or words. The more self-effacing one is, the more he is assisted in the Cause of God; and the more meek and humble, the nearer is he to God.

order.why: Consider the supplied account of the institution’s historical development.
Read the 1957 clarification of rank and assistance to National Assemblies.
shortened: The Rank, and Position of the Hands of the Cause, are superior to the position of the National Assemblies.

Because the Guardian has restrained the Hands at this time, and given as one of their functions, aiding the National bodies in winning the goals of the Ten Year Crusade, the National bodies should not misunderstand the true position of the Hands. They should report to the Hands, where teaching assistance is needed, etc., so the Hands, and their Auxiliary Boards, may be of the greatest assistance.

order.why: Keep the 1963 description of protective functions and required approval in its setting.
Read the 1968 procedures as a historical institutional instruction.
shortened: The authority of expulsion and reinstatement will be exercised by the Hands of Cause of God, subject in each instance to the approval of the Universal House of Justice. When a member of the Continental Boards of Counsellors learns of any incipient Covenant-breaking, the matter should be reported without delay with the matter. A copy of the report should be sent to the Hands in the Holy Land and to the other members of the Board.

order.why: Compare the 1964 separation from elected administrative service with earlier temporary arrangements.
End with the supplied account of consultation, representation, and spiritual inspiration across continents.

questions: What does the image of a hand suggest about the relationship between distinction and service?
How are learning, character, teaching, and protection connected in the duties described here?
What can the practical instructions about financial support and care reveal about institutional relationships?
How does attention to historical setting help explain the different arrangements concerning assemblies?
How does First Peter 5:2–3 illuminate leadership through willingness and example while retaining a different institutional setting?
What qualities make service a source of unity and spiritual encouragement for others?

references.label: 1 · 1 Peter 5:2–3 · Oversight through willing service and example
references.note: The King James Version counsels those tending a community to serve willingly, without pursuing gain or acting as lords over others, and to provide an example. Compare these ethical concerns with the compilation’s account of humility, detachment, learning, and service. This is a comparison of responsibilities and conduct, not an identification of Christian elders with the Baha’i institution of the Hands.

subjects.displayTitle: Holy days: remembrance becoming a shared way of life
subjects.introduction: Naw-Rúz, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá writes, must find expression in life, or it is like any other day. That warning sets the measure for every holy day: a date returning on the calendar is nothing until it becomes generosity to kindred and the poor, a table spread for friends, song and Tablets read aloud, work set aside, lamps lit by hand at a shrine. Bahá’u’lláh shaped the year so that it teaches this rhythm. Nineteen months carry the names of divine attributes; the Days of Há open a season of giving that leads into the Fast, and the Fast opens into the feast of the New Year; the twelve days of Ridván recall the garden where a Revelation was announced. Mourning has its hours too, so that the martyrdom of the Báb and the ascension of Bahá’u’lláh stay present in a community’s memory. The dates were settled over decades in letters that defer, adjust and explain, a history rather than a rule for today. Leviticus shows a festival joining harvest, rest and rejoicing so that later generations remember a deliverance [1]. From here the path leads to the Nineteen-Day Feast, the day of rest, the discipline of fasting, and the gatherings in which remembrance becomes a shared way of life.
subjects.arc: Begin with a holy day expressed in action, explore generosity and remembrance, and read the calendar’s forms within their historical and devotional settings.

order.why: Read the Aqdas passages joining generosity, restraint, celebration, and the ordering of months.
shortened: It behoveth the people of Baha, throughout these days, to provide good cheer for themselves, their kindred and, beyond them, the poor and needy, and with joy and exultation to hail and glorify their Lord, to sing His praise and magnify His Name; and when they end --these days of giving that precede the season of restraint--let them enter upon the Fast.
The number of months in a year, appointed in the Book of God, is nineteen. Of these the first hath been adorned with this Name which overshadoweth the whole of creation.

order.why: Open with the need for Naw-Ruz to have expression in life.
Consider a feast with physical food, spiritual conversation, and joyful fellowship.
Ask what lasting result a celebration might yield.
shortened: The program of such fête days must be so prepared as to yield a permanent result.

order.why: Read joy through music, song, and gladness.
Consider the intercalary days as preparation of the heart.
shortened: All the days have been honoured, O my God, by the arrival of the days upon which Thou hast conferred the name of Ha, each of which Thou hast made a herald and a messenger announcing unto the people the advent of the days on which Thou didst enjoin Thy creation and Thy people to observe the Fast. Thus may every soul prepare himself to behold these days and appoint a place for them in his heart and purify it by Thy Name, the Lord, for their appearance.

order.why: Read generosity during the Days of Ha.
Join the close of fasting with the Naw-Ruz prayer.
shortened: Praised be Thou, O my God, that Thou hast ordained Naw-Ruz as a festival unto those who have observed the fast for love of Thee and abstained from all that is abhorrent unto Thee.

order.why: Consider Naw-Ruz as a day made new in experience.
Explains the duration, observance and work prohibitions of the Most Great Festival.
Read the image of a divine Naw-Ruz.
Hear the call to remembrance and loving-kindness.
shortened: O Firuz! Hearken unto the call of the All-Merciful on this Naw-Ruz wherein all things have been adorned with the raiment of My remembrance and the garment of thy Lord's loving-kindness, the Bestower, the Bountiful.

order.why: Keep the greeting and Persian festival background within the letter’s setting.
shortened: O ye heralds of the Kingdom of God:

A few days ago an epistle was written to those divine believers, but because these days are the days of Naw-Ruz, you have come to my mind and I am sending you this greeting for this glorious feast. All the days are blessed, but this feast is the national fete of Persia. The Persians have been holding it for several thousand years past.

order.why: Read the reported seasonal account of the two equinoxes.
Consider the reported account of spring and the traditional story of Jamshid.
Keep the reported historical claim concerning Persian victory attributed.
Read recollection of celebration during Baha’u’llah’s lifetime.
shortened: During the days of the Blessed Perfection we celebrated this National New year's day with great elaboration and festivity ...
The Newyear's day is a day of pleasure and delight.

order.why: Place rejoicing beside the remembered intensity of mourning.
shortened: Today is the Feast of Naw-Ruz. Our festivals are most magnificent, having no equal among all peoples. Likewise, our days of mourning are most intense. However, when we were in this world with the Blessed Beauty, we would celebrate the feast during those blessed days.

order.why: Consider Ridvan’s joy amid exile.
Read the festival through the appearance of the Hidden.
shortened: This is the Day whereon He Who is the Hidden and the Unseen appeared before the eyes of all creation. All glory be to that which God hath bestowed upon us!

order.why: Hear the language of bounty encompassing existence.
shortened: O joy! This is the Festival of God that hath appeared from the horizon of transcendent grace. This is the Festival wherein all things have been adorned with the robe of names, and bounty hath encompassed all existence, of the former and latter generations. O joy! This is the Festival of God that hath dawned from the holy and gleaming Dayspring.

order.why: Read the prayer for the dawn of Ridvan.
shortened: O my God! Praise be unto Thee that the dawn of Thy Ridvan Festival hath broken, and that therein hath prospered whosoever hath turned unto Thee, O our Lord, the All-Merciful.

order.why: Consider a feast centered on the recitation of Tablets.
shortened: Thou didst wish to celebrate the Day of Ridvan with a feast, and to have those present on that day engage in reciting Tablets with delight and joy, and thou didst request me to send thee a letter to be read on that day.

order.why: Read the response to the question of particular festival readings.
Hear the invitation to sing in praise.
shortened: O spiritual nightingale, sing a melody with the divine sweet tone on this Ridvan Festival in praise and glorification of the All-Merciful Beauty, that the song of "O Glory of the Most Glorious" may reach the ears of this servant.

order.why: Read the encouragement of poetry and melodious recitation.
shortened: O thou nightingale in the Rose-garden of Significances!

The poetry that thou hast composed on the occasion of the Feast of the Ridvan is wonderful, eloquent, fluent and sweet. With a melodious voice it should be sung during the Days of the Ridvan and the believers and maidservants of the Merciful must listen.

order.why: Consider music and celebration on the grounds of the House of Worship.
Read the practical choice of Ridvan for a wider gathering in Chicago.
shortened: O friends and maidservants of the All-Merciful! If your intention is to arrange a general gathering in Chicago during Naw-Ruz, where people from all directions will be present and discussions will be held regarding the Mashriqu'l-Adhkar, and the oneness of the world of humanity will be proclaimed, and the divine teachings will be discussed, and the counsels of the Blessed Beauty will be explained and elucidated, it would be better if this event were to take place during the Festival of Ridvan, for Ridvan is the Most Great Festival and the weather is perfectly moderate.

order.why: Consider a local Ridvan celebration as a heavenly banquet.
shortened: O ye who are longing for the countenance of that Kind Beloved!
Praise be to God that the city of Qazvin has become such a banquet hall of the highest heaven that in the Festival of Ridvan the heavenly feast descended from the celestial kingdom.

order.why: Read the remembered delight of a village celebration.
shortened: O friends of this imprisoned servant! His Honor Taraz and His Honor Ali-Akbar spent the Ridvan days in that blessed village in joy and delight, and they described the spiritual pleasure and divine sweetness of those days, saying that praise be to God, we were hand in hand with the divine friends, and intoxicated with the wine of the All-Merciful, enchanted by that radiant countenance and enraptured by those scattered tresses, and were infinitely joyous and glad.

order.why: Keep the related praise of joyful observance in its setting.
shortened: O ye steadfast ones! You celebrated the festival days in that blessed village with the utmost joy and gladness, and attained happiness and success.

order.why: Consider gathering near the Shrine within the account of Ridvan.
shortened: O you who are firm in the Covenant and servant of the Testament! On the Day of Ridvan, a vast pavilion was erected in an elevated location facing the Holy Shrine, and at the time of visitation the friends of God gathered and the divine assembly was present.

order.why: Read the particular ninth-day invitation within the prison setting.
shortened: This is the ninth day of Ridvan, O my God, and on this day one of Thy loved ones hath, as a token of his love for Thy Beauty and in the eagerness of his devotion to Thee, invited Him Who is the Manifestation of Thy Self and the Dayspring of Thy glory to leave His room in the prison for another.

order.why: Attend to the historical reply about Ridvan’s twelve days.
shortened: And regarding your question about the number of days of Ridvan - it is twelve days, and its first day is that same day two hours before sunset.

order.why: Read the detailed reckoning of its beginning within the letter’s occasion.
Consider the distinction among the three days on which work is forbidden.
shortened: On the thirty-second day, at the time of the afternoon prayer, the Ancient Beauty entered the Garden of Ridvan. That moment marks the beginning of the Most Great Festival, and that day together with the second day of the Festival are reckoned as one day. It is strictly forbidden in the Book to engage in work on the first, ninth and twelfth days, but there is no objection to working on the other days.

order.why: Keep the reply concerning the first afternoon within its calendrical context.
Retain the affirmation of a correspondent’s reckoning without supplying an unstated date.
Read the distinction between required and additional abstention from work.
Consider shared rest and gathering in the reported account.
shortened: In the sacred laws of God in every cycle and dispensation, there are blessed feasts, holidays and workless days. On such days no kind of occupation, commerce, industry, agriculture, or the like, is allowed. All work is unlawful. All must enjoy themselves, gather together, hold general meetings, become as one assembly, so that the oneness, unity and harmony of the people may be demonstrated in the eyes of all.

order.why: Read the nine holy days in the historical calendars supplied.
Retain the separate enumeration without converting its dates.
Consider the exception for shepherds so that animals do not go hungry.
Read the explicit distinction between existing practice and later implementation.
shortened: Regarding what you wrote about the Day of the Declaration of the Bab (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him), it is recorded in the Questions and Answers that the Day of Kamal falls in the Month of 'Azamat, and the Day of Martyrdom falls on the Day of Sultan in the Month of Rahmat. This is definitive text which no matter can contradict. This will be implemented later. However, since in the blessed days these two holy days were observed on the fifth of Jumada I and the twenty-eighth of Sha'ban, and the loved ones would present themselves in the Most Holy Court, expressing joy on the Day of Declaration and showing intense grief and sorrow in the countenance of the Blessed Beauty on the Day of Martyrdom, we therefore continue to observe these two days on these two dates until now. But what is in the texts will be implemented later.

order.why: Consider the relation of solar and lunar reckonings.
Keep the reported reference to future decisions by the House of Justice in its setting.
Read the historical explanation of differing regional reckonings.
Consider the reported permission and its reference to future institutional decisions.
Read the permission to use a calendar in determining Arabic months.
Consider wisdom and the temporary deferral of observance.
shortened: As to what was mentioned regarding the Holy Days, they are the first and second of Muharram. However, wisdom does not at present permit their observance, for the heedless party--that is, the Shi'ih--have formed and continue to form other notions. Therefore this ordinance and other ordinances are for future days, and their time shall come. Thus hath spoken the tongue of our Lord, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise.

order.why: Read a particular festival’s suspension as an example of that historical wisdom.
shortened: In all conditions, all the friends who have truly partaken of the Most Pure Wine and are focused on the Greatest Scene must observe wisdom. The matter of wisdom is mentioned and accepted before God to such a degree that this year the Most Great Festival of the Birth was not celebrated. He said: "We have prohibited this festival to exalt the station of wisdom and to elevate its rank." From this comprehensive, decisive and blessed word, the significance of wisdom becomes clear and evident.

order.why: Keep the Bab’s numerical scheme within its own revealed setting.
Read the supplied names and structure of days and months without silently correcting its reckoning.
shortened: The year has been fixed at nineteen months, and each month at nineteen days.

It has been ordained that these five days, which are called the Days of Ha and the Days of Giving that precede the Fast, should be placed before the month of fasting, and the month of fasting is the last month of the year, while Naw-Ruz is the first day of the year.

As for the names of those nineteen months, they are as follows: First, the Month of Splendor; Second, the Month of Glory; Third, the Month of Beauty; Fourth, the Month of Grandeur; Fifth, the Month of Light; Sixth, the Month of Mercy; Seventh, the Month of Words; Eighth, the Month of Perfection; Ninth, the Month of Names; Tenth, the Month of Might; Eleventh, the Month of Will; Twelfth, the Month of Knowledge; Thirteenth, the Month of Power; Fourteenth, the Month of Speech; Fifteenth, the Month of Questions; Sixteenth, the Month of Honor; Seventeenth, the Month of Sovereignty; Eighteenth, the Month of Dominion; Nineteenth, the Month of Loftiness.

order.why: Keep the reported midnight answer distinct from authoritative guidance for present observance.
Read the belief about the moon as a reported person’s misconception, not the speaker’s calendrical teaching.
shortened: For example he firmly believed that when he grows very old suddenly he will be rejuvenated and become a youth as handsome as "Joseph", or he believed because the Bab has divided the year into 19 months in the future something will happen to the moon that instead of rising and setting 28 days in the month, it will rise and set only 19 times.

order.why: Consider the personification of Naw-Ruz in the Bab’s address.
Read the account of the four festivals with its catalogue’s attribution uncertainty.
shortened: In the Book of Aqdas, the Most Exalted Pen has ordained four festivals for all the peoples of the world, wherein the followers of Baha should meet and associate with one another with love for God, to such extent as does not contravene the wisdom revealed in the Tablets of God.

The first is the Day of Baha of the month of Baha, which is the ancient Naw-Ruz and the Festival of the Fast, marking the beginning of months and years, wherein the bounties of God are made manifest on that day beloved of all worlds.

The second is the Most Great Festival, which is the king of festivals, being those days when the Ancient Beauty emerged from the Most Great House and illumined the Najibiyyih Garden with the light of His countenance.

order.why: Keep the Declaration of the Bab central in the response about Abdu’l-Baha’s birthday.
shortened: Regarding the birth of this servant, which also happened on that day, this a proof of the favors and bounties of God toward this servant. However, this Blessed Day must be known as the Day of the Declaration of His Highness the Supreme (the Bab) and the beginning of the effulgence of the Sun of Reality. You must on this account be engaged in rejoicing, happiness and gladness.

order.why: Read the fellowship of the Bab’s birthday gathering.
shortened: O friends and handmaidens of the Merciful! Praise be to God that you have gathered together in utmost affection and love, and on the Birth Day of the Exalted One (the Bab) you attained perfect fellowship and joy, and engaged in the mention of God.

order.why: Consider a feast and visitation offered in another person’s name.
shortened: On the day of the Birth [of the Bab] a feast was held in the name of that handmaiden, and the ladies all visited the Holy Shrine on her behalf.

order.why: Hear the congratulation for a birthday celebration.
shortened: O ye who are firm in the Covenant! The congratulations for the blessed Festival of the Birth of His Holiness the Exalted One arrived, indicating that those friends and handmaidens of the All-Merciful arranged a gathering, organized a feast, held a celebration, and with utmost joy brought that day to its close.

order.why: Retain the greeting for the birth of the Greatest Name.
shortened: Now the purpose is congratulations for this glorious festival, the Day of the Birth of the Greatest Name.

order.why: Read the birthday through the image of descending bounty.
Hear the brief greeting for the blessed morning.
Follow the detailed account of a Declaration celebration and visitation.
shortened: Yesterday, which was the fifth of Jumada al-Awwal, the Day of the Declaration of His Holiness the Exalted One, they pitched the pavilion near the Holy Shrine and Blessed Tomb (may my spirit be a sacrifice for its dust), and in perfect joy and fragrance the feast of happiness was arranged.

After the recitation of special tablets, prayers, odes and praises of the Ancient Beauty (may my spirit be sacrificed for His loved ones) and His Holiness the Exalted One (may my soul be sacrificed for Him), and after conversation and counsel, the table was spread and lunch was eaten in your memory. Afterwards tea was served around, and then all the friends, with complete humility and submissiveness, faced the Holy Shrine and with utter meekness and lowliness we all attained the honor of kissing the Sacred Threshold.

The visitation continued until about an hour after sunset, and I lit all the lamps of the Pure Shrine with my own hand, and on your behalf I perfumed my face and hair with the dust of that fragrant and sweet-scented threshold.

order.why: Consider the joy produced by feasts of declaration and regular gathering.
shortened: The great feast that you celebrated on the occasion of the appearance of His Highness, the Bab, likewise the feasts of nineteen days, produced great rejoicing in the hearts of the believers.

order.why: Read the acknowledgment of a banquet for the Declaration.
shortened: You have written regarding the Feast of the declaration of His Holiness the Bab, that you have celebrated a banquet and arranged a blessed gathering.

order.why: Consider celebration as renewing guidance.
Hear praise for character shown during the Hasan-Abad celebration.
shortened: O two brothers like two celestial bodies! Jinab-i-Amin has offered the utmost praise for your strength of heart, loftiness of purpose and nobility of character at the feast and celebration in Hasan-Abad on the blessed Day of the Declaration of His Holiness the Exalted One, may my spirit be sacrificed for Him, and with complete humility has requested the writing of this letter.

order.why: Read Naw-Ruz fellowship in Germany.
shortened: O sons and daughters of the Kingdom! Your letter written on Naw-Ruz Day in the gathering of friends was received.

Its reading brought the utmost joy and delight, for praise be to God, in Germany the servants and handmaidens of the Merciful arranged a gathering of fellowship and love on Naw-Ruz Day, and made their spirits fragrant with the life-giving breeze of the Abha Paradise, and were engaged in the mention of the King of the Kingdom, the Lord of Hosts.

order.why: Consider the joy conveyed by news of observance.
shortened: O true friends of this Prisoner! News of your joyous festivities during the days of the Holy Day arrived and brought the utmost delight and joy.

order.why: Retain the personal response to details of Naw-Ruz.
shortened: You had written about the details of Naw-Ruz and it brought infinite joy.

order.why: Read the appreciation of a festival program.
shortened: The program of the Naw-Ruz festival was received and caused utmost joy.

order.why: Connect Naw-Ruz with the interment of the Bab’s remains.
shortened: O spiritual friends! The greatest glad-tidings is that the pure, luminous, and holy remains of His Holiness the Exalted One (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him), after being moved from place to place for sixty years due to the control of enemies and fear of the hostile ones, never finding rest or repose, through the grace of the Blessed Beauty was finally established, on the day of Naw-Ruz with utmost ceremony and perfect majesty and beauty, in the sacred casket at the most exalted spot on Mount Carmel.
This gathering took place on Naw-Ruz and definitive arrangements were made, with glad tidings telegraphed to the Holy Land.

order.why: Read the related remembrance of the resting place on Mount Carmel.
Keep the account of the Shrine’s construction in its particular setting.
shortened: The sacred shrine of His Holiness the Exalted One (may my spirit be sacrificed for Him) is rising day by day in the intense heat. Soon a magnificent grand level surrounded by multiple spaces will be completed with perfect solidity.

order.why: Read the reported sacred associations of Carmel.
shortened: No other spot in the world is as pleasant and vivifying as this realm, nor can rival it in beauty and majesty. On this mountain (Carmel), the Prophets of Israel spent Their nights in prayer and supplication. Its soil has been blessed by the footsteps of the Prophets.

order.why: Consider the reported spiritual value of visiting the Shrine.
Read the change from meeting a living presence to visiting a tomb.
shortened: During the Feast Days one is reminded more forcibly of the Days of Baha'u'llah, more particularly the Days of Rizwan. Consider how different it is now! During the life-time of the Blessed Perfection on Rizwan days we used to go into His Holy Presence; now during those self-same days we go visit His radiant Tomb....

order.why: Make room for prayerful mourning and remembrance.
Consider visitation of the martyrs’ graves on a commemorative day.
shortened: On the 28th of Sha'ban, the day of martyrdom of His Holiness the Exalted One (may my soul be sacrificed for Him), a group of divine friends should visit on behalf of this servant the illumined graves of the martyrs and fragrant tombs of those near to the Divine Threshold in Tehran, as representatives of Abdul-Baha.

order.why: Close the linked sequence with a gathering devoted to remembrance at the Ascension.
End with the supplied historical overview of the calendar, retaining its distinct authorship and wording.

questions: What would make a holy day a renewed experience rather than simply a date returning?
How do generosity, fasting, celebration, and remembrance work together in the yearly rhythm?
What do shared rest, hospitality, music, and conversation contribute to a community’s life?
How can joy and mourning each sustain gratitude and a living relationship with history?
How does Leviticus 23:39–43 connect celebration with the memory carried by later generations?
What becomes clearer when historical arrangements and reported customs are distinguished from the purposes of observance?

references.label: 1 · Leviticus 23:39–43 · Festival, rest, and remembrance across generations
references.note: The King James Version connects the festival with harvest, rest, rejoicing, and dwelling in booths so that later generations remember Israel’s departure from Egypt. Compare the relationship of practice and memory with the compilation’s accounts of holy days. The calendars and sacred histories remain distinct; consider how recurring actions can transmit gratitude and a shared sense of purpose.
